skills.content:
---
name: bot-cartoon-icons
description: >-
  Use this when making, refreshing, or setting cartoon profile pictures for a
  person's Grok bots in their chosen style.
---
# Bot cartoon icons

1. Load the owner's saved toon style card from memory (art style, framing, character type, shared theme, colors, mood, personal touches, limits, options-or-pick, refresh rules). If there isn't one, run the getting-started interview first.
2. List the bots to draw: read /home/box/agent-data/agents/*/profile.json for names and descriptions, or use the bots the owner named.
3. For each bot, design one character that fits its job and the style card. Never depict a real person or their likeness, and never copy copyrighted characters ("inspired by" a style is fine). For bots named after real people or TV characters, draw a themed object or animal instead.
4. GenerateImage with aspect_ratio 1:1: a plain background, the character centered, readable at avatar size, and no text unless the card allows it. If the card says to show options, make 2 or 3 per bot and let the owner pick.
5. With Shell (Python PIL), center-crop and resize each image to a 512x512 PNG at /workspace/bot-avatars/<kebab-bot-name>.png. That shared folder is the only place other bots can read; images left in your own store or assets folder are invisible to them.
6. Set your own picture with UpdateAvatar. Each bot can only set its own picture, so SendToAgent each other bot (priority true): ask it to call UpdateAvatar with action set and its /workspace/bot-avatars path, not to message the owner, and to reply 'avatar set' (priority false) or say what failed. Redo any that fail.
7. Build a lineup contact sheet (a grid with each name under its picture) at /workspace/bot-avatars/lineup.png and show it to the owner.
8. For redos ("make the calendar bot grumpier") or newly created bots, draw just those, in the same style.
9. Seasonal refreshes, if the owner wants them, run as a routine on the dates they chose.

skills.content:
---
name: toon-maker-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of a Toon Maker (bot
  cartoon icon) assistant, to learn their style and draw their first icons.
---
Introduce yourself in one line: you draw fun cartoon profile pictures for all their Grok bots and keep them fresh.

Ask one question at a time, each as a widget with a few options plus a typed answer, and save each answer to memory as part of their toon style card:
1. What art style? Examples: Peanuts-inspired, Simpsons-inspired, Garbage Pail Kids-inspired, comic book, anime, Pixar-style 3D, retro 1950s, pixel art, claymation, watercolor, or an artist they love.
2. Face only, head and shoulders, or full body?
3. What should the characters be: animals, robots, objects that match each bot's job, superheroes or villains, monsters, or a mix?
4. Should the whole cast share one theme (a superhero team, sports team, pirate crew or office coworkers), or should each bot be its own thing?
5. Colors: one color per bot, one brand palette, or a background color they like?
6. What mood: cute, goofy, gross-out funny, heroic, or professional?
7. Any hobbies, favorite teams or hometown touches to sneak in as props?
8. Anything off-limits? Is text or initials on the image OK?
9. Should you show 2 or 3 options per bot, or just pick one and set it?
10. Should the icons be redrawn seasonally, like Halloween or the holidays, or only when they ask?

Then draw one sample bot and confirm the look. Once they like it, run the bot-cartoon-icons skill for all their bots. If they want seasonal refreshes, create a routine for those dates.
